title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: Civil Disobedience and Beyond

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Gandhiji's years in South Africa and the India of 1915 shaped his entry into Indian politics.
Explain why Gandhiji's Banaras Hindu University speech of February 1916 was both a statement of fact and a statement of intent.

topics.title: The Making and Unmaking of Non-cooperation

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how the localised struggles of 1917-18 and the Rowlatt Satyagraha made Gandhiji a national leader.
Explain the aims of Non-cooperation and the reasons for joining it with the Khilafat Movement.
Analyse why Gandhiji called off Non-cooperation after the Chauri Chaura incident of February 1922.
Explain how Gandhiji's dress and the charkha helped him identify with the labouring poor.
Interpret what the rumours about Gandhiji's powers reveal about how peasants saw him.
Describe how Congress organisation, followers and supporters broadened Gandhian nationalism.

topics.title: The Salt Satyagraha: Purna Swaraj and Dandi

concepts.learning_objective: State the significance of the Lahore Congress of 1929 and the observance of Independence Day in 1930.
Explain why Gandhiji chose the salt monopoly as the target of the Dandi March.
Compare the wider streams of protest during Civil Disobedience with those of Non-cooperation.

topics.title: Dialogues: Round Table Conferences and Separate Electorates

concepts.learning_objective: State why the Salt March was a notable event in the national movement.
Explain the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and why the Round Table dialogues remained inconclusive.
Compare the views of Gandhiji and Ambedkar on separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.

topics.title: Quit India and the Last Heroic Days

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the failure of the Cripps Mission and the mass character of the Quit India Movement.
Explain how the 1946 elections and Direct Action Day led to political polarisation and Partition.
Evaluate Gandhiji's work for communal harmony after Independence and the response to his death.

topics.title: Knowing Gandhi: Sources for the Nationalist Movement

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse what private letters and autobiographies reveal and the care needed in reading them.
Interpret the Fortnightly Reports of the Home Department as a colonial source.
Explain why contemporary newspapers are useful but not unprejudiced sources.
